Found a bug: `[Export]` properties from external assemblies show up in the Inspector (correct names and types), but display C# default values (0, 0.0, `<null>`) instead of initializer values, and can't be edited.

Main project scripts work fine — issue is specific to referenced assemblies.

The discovery side works — types are found, `GetGodotPropertyList()` runs, `[GlobalClass]` works. The problem is likely in the property get/set bridge (`_Set`, `_Get`, `GetGodotPropertyDefaultValues`) not connecting for types outside the main assembly, probably somewhere in `CSharpInstance` creation or managed callback dispatch.

Lifecycle methods (`_Ready`, `_Process`) work. `[GlobalClass]` works. But broken `[Export]` is a blocker for real usage.

Investigating — would appreciate any pointers on how property dispatch resolves types across assemblies.

### Update: [Export] properties now working for all assembly types Found and fixed the root cause of the `[Export]` issue reported above. **Problem:** `GetGodotPropertyDefaultValues()` and other editor-only generated methods are wrapped in `#if TOOLS`. Projects using `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` (instead of `Godot.NET.Sdk`) don't define `TOOLS`, so these methods are compiled out. The properties appear in the Inspector (via `GetGodotPropertyList()` which has no `#if TOOLS` guard) but show default C# values (0, null) and can't be edited. **Solution:** Projects using `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` with `Godot.SourceGenerators` must define `GODOT` and `TOOLS` in their build configuration. The example project's `Directory.Build.props` now includes this for all sub-projects automatically. NuGet packages must also be built with `TOOLS` defined. This is a **user configuration requirement**, not an engine bug — `Godot.NET.Sdk` handles this automatically, but `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` projects need explicit defines. Updated the [example project](https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference) accordingly. Also fixed CI failures: - `ScriptPathAttribute.SourceFile` used nullable annotation (`string?`) without `#nullable enable` context — changed to `string` - `is_assembly_backed` variable unused in `template_release` builds (only used in `TOOLS_ENABLED`/`DEBUG_ENABLED` blocks) — added `[[maybe_unused]]` ##### Node from Microsoft.NET.Sdk-based project ##### Node from Godot.NET.Sdk-based project
That'd be so nice to have! This is a standard practice in enterprise C#, having this in Godot would make project layout much cleaner.

### Update: Transitive dependencies now supported

Discovered that scripts from transitive dependencies weren't showing up in the Add Node dialog. For example, if you have a dependency chain like:

```
MainProject → InTreeModule → SomeNuGetPackage
```

The NuGet package's scripts would be found and registered internally, but never actually loaded as script resources — so they were invisible in the editor.

The fix was a one-liner: I was only proactively loading scripts with `csharp://` paths, but transitive `res://` dependencies (like a project referenced by another project) were silently skipped. Now all scripts from referenced assemblies are loaded regardless of path scheme.

The [example project](https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference) now tests all the transitive chains:

- **TransitiveDependencyModule** — an in-tree project referenced by InTreeGodotSdkModule (Project → Project)
- **TransitiveNuGetFromProject** — a NuGet package referenced by InTreeModule (Project → NuGet)  
- **TransitiveNuGetFromNuGet** — a NuGet package referenced by ExternalNuGetModule (NuGet → NuGet)

All three show up correctly in Add Node with working `[Export]` properties.
How much of this work is usabe and relevant with the GDExtension-based C# backend that's supposedly being worked on?

Good question. I looked at the [godot-dotnet](https://github.com/raulsntos/godot-dotnet) codebase to check.

godot-dotnet uses a different registration model — no script paths, no `ScriptPathAttribute`, no runtime assembly scanning for types. A source generator finds `[GodotClass]` types at compile time via Roslyn's `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` and emits explicit `GodotRegistry.RegisterClass<T>()` calls).

**The same multi-assembly problem exists there.** `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` triggers on syntax nodes — it finds types declared in the current compilation's source files. Types from referenced assemblies are metadata symbols with no syntax nodes, so they're invisible to the generator. If you have a library with `[GodotClass]` types via `<ProjectReference>`, the main project's source generator won't see them and no `RegisterClass<T>()` calls will be emitted for them. There's no cross-assembly discovery mechanism — I searched the codebase and found nothing.

(godot-dotnet does have a `DisableGodotEntryPointGenerationAttribute` for manual entry points, and a `PluginLoader` that loads extensions at runtime — but neither solves the `<ProjectReference>` multi-assembly case. The `PluginLoader` loads one assembly at a time by explicit path and doesn't scan for `[GodotClass]` types in dependencies.)

**How much of this work is directly usable?** Not much code-wise — the architectures are too different. The `csharp://` scheme, `ScriptPathAttribute`, runtime directory scanning — none of that exists in godot-dotnet. But the core problem is identical: types in referenced assemblies are invisible to registration. The patterns this PR establishes (discovering dependencies, proactively registering external types, giving them stable identities) are the same patterns godot-dotnet will need to solve.

Either way, this PR fixes a real limitation for users of the current backend, which is the only shipping one and will remain so for a while.
@raulsntos Hey, just checking in - this has been open for a couple of weeks. Let me know if there's anything I should change or if the approach needs rethinking.

Thanks @pcloves — both reports were real issues. Fixed on the latest push. **1. Custom Resources from PackageReference disappearing.** Your debugging pointed straight at `EditorFileSystem::_remove_invalid_global_class_names` - it was purging every `csharp://` class right after startup registered them, because its "valid class names" set is built by walking `res://` only. Fix: skip `csharp://` paths in the purge. Fix: 8f5f4ada59 **2. `EditorNode::get_singleton()` being null during early registration.** Same thing - you spotted that `_register_csharp_global_class` runs from `ScriptServer::init_languages()` well before `memnew(EditorNode)`, so the icon-path / class-name setters on `EditorData` were silently skipped. Fix: queue the entries when `EditorNode` isn't ready yet, flush them from `_editor_init_callback` once it is. Fix: 74ee3801f0 Also rebased the PR onto current master so the conflict banner clears. Most of that is just picking up upstream's move of `ResourceFormatLoaderCSharpScript` into the new `csharp_script_resource_format.cpp`. If you want to reproduce both scenarios, full steps are here: https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference/blob/master/TESTING.md Thanks again for the detailed debugging.

Thank @matelq  for the quick response and for fixing the issue. I've tested it and it works. Although I didn't use your latest commit, my own fix ended up being exactly the same as yours – ha.

There's one more issue I'd like to bring up, even though it seems unrelated to this feature: I have a custom `"csharp://"` Resource named `Timer`, and it also doesn't show up in the Create Resource dialog. I've tracked down the reason – in [CreateDialog::_fill_type_list()](https://github.com/matelq/godot/blob/58520950da5e1a71f76930507c8ac635275f81d5/editor/gui/create_dialog.cpp#L90), the data source includes both `ClassDB` and `ScriptServer`. My `csharp:// Timer` exists in `ScriptServer`, but coincidentally `ClassDB` also has a `Timer` (I'm guessing it's the built-in [Timer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_timer.html) node). However, that `Timer` in `ClassDB` isn't a Resource, so it gets hidden by [CreateDialog::_should_hide_type()](https://github.com/matelq/godot/blob/58520950da5e1a71f76930507c8ac635275f81d5/editor/gui/create_dialog.cpp#L187).

I can work around this by renaming the `csharp://` Resource, so it's not a blocking issue.

@pcloves Glad it's working, and thanks for testing.

The `Timer` case isn't multi-assembly-specific - based on the codepath you already traced, any `class_name`/`[GlobalClass]` that shadows a built-in type should hit the same `CreateDialog` filtering, regardless of language or assembly (I haven't reproduced the GDScript case myself). Worth a separate issue, but out of scope here. Rename workaround is a reasonable stopgap.

---

I've tested this PR for a while, and it works normally for editor case, however running exported game with multiple csproj will immediately crash. Looks like when calling `LookupScriptsInReferencedAssemblies` in game start, gd mono cache has not been constructed yet, so that any `OS.IsStdOutVerbose()` call will lead to a crash. Furthermore, loading cs script here is also not allowed due to same reason, this should only be called in editor. I believe some guards like `NativeFuncs.godotsharp_dotnet_module_is_initialized().ToBool() && Engine.IsEditorHint()` is necessary here. By manually patching this I can make exported game work normally.

@neomoth Your MRP isn't hitting the engine bug it's a csproj config problem. SubProject is on Microsoft.NET.Sdk, which doesn't set GodotProjectDir or the GODOT;TOOLS defines that Godot.NET.Sdk provides. Without the first, the script-path generator throws and emits nothing; without TOOLS, the default-value generator is compiled out that's why your 35.53f reads back as 0. Attached is your MRP with that fixed and pointed at the fork's 4.7.2.2 packages, plus a screenshot of it running: the subproject's [Export]s are editable, persist through save, and print correctly at runtime. Note the config fix alone isn't enough on stock Godot — there the path still comes out as res://../SubProject/..., which is what this PR is about.
